battle.name: 波蘭戰役
battle.brief: 波蘭戰役是德國與蘇聯於1939年9月共同入侵波蘭的軍事衝突，標誌二戰全面爆發。作戰期間，德軍部署四號坦克（PanzerkampfwagenIV）為主力裝甲，實行快速突破與包圍戰術。

kit.name: 四號坦克
kit.history: 四號坦克是德軍在二戰初期的主力中坦，負責支援步兵與對抗敵方裝甲，並參與閃擊戰術的實施。

countries: 1939年9月1日凌晨4時45分，納粹德國在「白色方案」（Fall Weiss）指導下，從東普魯士、西部波蘭邊境以及斯洛伐克三路同時發動侵略。德國國防軍（Heer）投入了約56個師，其中包括9個裝甲師與6個摩托化師，隸屬於北方集團軍（Heeresgruppe Nord）和南方集團軍（Heeresgruppe Süd），合計兵力約88萬人。與此同時，蘇聯於9月17日在納粹-蘇聯互不侵犯條約的秘密議定書基礎上，出動約25個師，合計約50萬人，從東部的比亞韋斯托克-沃倫斯克一線進入波蘭。斯洛伐克亦派出了3個步兵師，支援德軍的左翼行動。波蘭方面，軍隊編制約30個師，總兵力約45萬人，主要部署於維斯瓦河、桑河及波茲南等防線，但因裝備老舊與指揮失調，無法形成有效抵抗。
countriesEn: On September 1, 1939 at 04:45, Nazi Germany, under the directives of Operation Fall Weiss, launched a three‑pronged invasion from East Prussia, the western Polish border and Slovakia. The German Heer committed roughly 56 divisions, including nine Panzer and six motorized divisions, under Army Group North (Heeresgruppe Nord) and Army Group South (Heeresgruppe Süd), totaling about 880,000 men. Simultaneously, on September 17 the Soviet Union, acting on the secret protocol of the Nazi‑Soviet Non‑Aggression Pact, entered Poland from the east along the Białystok‑Wołyńsk line with about 25 divisions, roughly 500,000 troops. Slovakia also contributed three infantry divisions to support the German left flank. The Polish forces, comprising roughly 30 divisions and about 450,000 men, were mainly positioned along the Vistula, San and Poznań lines, but outdated equipment and command failures prevented effective resistance.
people: 此役雙方主要指揮官包括德國的裝甲兵將領海因茨·古德里安（General der Panzertruppe Heinz Guderian），率領第19軍的快速兵團在波蘭走廊高速突破；北方集團軍司令威廉·克盧格上將（Generaloberst Wilhelm von Kluge）負責協調第4軍與第3裝甲師的行動；南方集團軍的弗朗茨·哈爾德上將（Generaloberst Franz Halder）則主導第10軍與第14軍的聯合進攻。波蘭方面，最高統帥愛德華·雷茲-希米格萊元帥（Marszałek Edward Rydz‑Śmigły）負責全域指揮，副官斯蒂芬·羅韋茨基（Grot）指揮「波茲南」軍第7師在布祖拉河展開激烈防守。蘇聯軍的指挥則由克萊門特·伏羅希洛夫元帥（Marszałek Kliment Woroszyłów）率領的西方軍區負責。
peopleEn: The principal commanders on both sides included German panzer leader General der Panzertruppe Heinz Guderian, who commanded the fast‑moving corps of the 19th Army in a rapid breakthrough through the Polish Corridor; Army Group North’s commander, Generaloberst Wilhelm von Kluge, coordinated the actions of the 4th Army and the 3rd Panzer Division; and Army Group South’s commander, Generaloberst Franz Halder, directed the joint offensive of the 10th and 14th Armies. On the Polish side, Marshal Edward Rydz‑Śmigły served as supreme commander, with his deputy, General Stefan Rowecki "Grot", leading the 7th Infantry Division of the Poznań Army in fierce defense along the Bzura River. Soviet forces were commanded by Marshal Kliment Woroszyłow of the Western Military District.
kits: 在武器裝備方面，德軍投入了大量1930年代已列裝的車輛與火力。裝甲兵力包括Panzerkampfwagen I（1 號坦克，配備2挺7.92 mm機槍）與II號坦克（配備20 mm機炮），以及稍後於1939年才少量交付的III號坦克（配37 mm短管炮）與IV號坦克（配75 mm長管炮），以及少量從捷克俘獲的35(t)與38(t)坦克。步兵則以Karabiner 98k步槍、7.92 mm MG 34機槍、7.5 cm leIG 18步兵炮、10.5 cm leFH 18輕型榴彈炮為主，另有8.8 cm Flak 18防空炮提供對地支援。空軍方面，Luftwaffe使用了Bf 109E戰鬥機、Bf 110C重型戰鬥機、He 111中型轟炸機與Ju 87“斯圖卡”俯衝轟炸機。波蘭軍隊則裝備了7TP輕型坦克（配12.7 mm機槍）與TK‑3小型坦克，配有7.92 mm wz.29步槍、7.92 mm Browning wz.30機槍、37 mm波福斯反戰車炮、75 mm山地步兵炮及105 mm榴彈炮，空中力量則有PZL P.11單翼戰鬥機、PZL P.24多用途戰鬥機與PZL P.37“洛斯”中型轟炸機。
kitsEn: In terms of weapons and equipment, the German forces fielded a large number of vehicles and firepower that had entered service in the 1930s. Their armored units comprised the Panzerkampfwagen I (a 2‑man tank armed with two 7.92 mm machine guns), the Panzerkampfwagen II (equipped with a 20 mm cannon), and a small number of the later‑introduced Panzerkampfwagen III (with a 37 mm short‑barreled gun) and Panzerkampfwagen IV (armed with a 75 mm long‑barreled gun), as well as a few captured Czech 35(t) and 38(t) tanks. Infantry relied primarily on the Karabiner 98k rifle, the 7.92 mm MG 34 machine gun, the 7.5 cm leIG 18 infantry gun, the 10.5 cm leFH 18 light howitzer, and the 8.8 cm Flak 18 anti‑aircraft gun for ground support. The Luftwaffe employed the Messerschmitt Bf 109E fighter, theBf 110C heavy fighter, the Heinkel He 111 medium bomber, and the Junkers Ju 87 “Stuka” dive‑bomber. The Polish forces were equipped with the 7TP light tank (armed with a 12.7 mm machine gun) and the TK‑3 tankette, as well as the 7.92 mm wz.29 rifle, the 7.92 mm Browning wz.30 machine gun, the 37 mm Bofors anti‑tank gun, the 75 mm mountain infantry gun, and the 105 mm howitzer. Their air arm consisted of the PZL P.11 sesquiplane fighter, the PZL P.24 multirole fighter, and the PZL P.37 “Łoś” medium bomber.
tactics: 德軍在波蘭的戰術以「閃電戰」為核心，首先由Panzer師在前線形成突破口，利用高速機動的裝甲縱隊突破波蘭薄弱的前哨，隨即由摩托化步兵師擴大突破口，並以Luftwaffe的Ju 87對敵軍集結點、道路與鐵路實施定點俯轟，削弱波蘭後勤與指揮結構。第19軍的摩托化兵團在古德里安的指揮下，於9月1日早晨僅用數小時即突破“波蘭走廊”北端的波蘭步兵師防線，並向東快速挺進。波蘭軍隊則採取了以河川為天然屏障的固定防禦，於維斯瓦河與桑河沿岸構築混凝土工事，並以騎兵旅作為快速反應力量試圖截斷突破的德軍縱隊，然而通訊裝備匱乏與缺乏空中支援，使反制行動屢屢受阻。
tacticsEn: German tactics in Poland were centered on the ‘Blitzkrieg’ concept: Panzer divisions first created a breach in the forward line, using high‑speed armored columns to overrun weak Polish outposts, after which motorized infantry divisions expanded the gap. The Luftwaffe supported the advance by employing Ju 87 Stukas to conduct precision dive‑bombing attacks on enemy concentrations, roads and railways, thereby degrading Polish logistics and command structures. Under Guderian’s command, the motorized corps of the 19th Army broke through the northern sector of the Polish Corridor in just a few hours on the morning of 1 September and pushed rapidly eastward. The Polish forces, by contrast, relied on static river‑based defenses, building concrete fortifications along the Vistula and San, and used cavalry brigades as rapid‑response units to try to cut off the German spearheads, but inadequate communications and lack of air cover repeatedly thwarted their counter‑attacks.
data: 戰役的時間線如下：1939年9月1日04:45，德軍首先轟炸格但斯克港的韋斯特普拉特，隨即在東普魯士與西利西亞兩線同步展開陸上部隊；9月3日，英法兩國對德宣戰，但西線并未立即發動實質性軍事行動。9月8日，德第4軍的第2裝甲師已逼近華沙市郊，華沙保衛戰正式打響。9月14日至19日，波蘭第7師與第15師在布祖拉河與德軍展開激烈交火，史稱“布祖拉戰役”。9月17日，蘇聯紅軍從東部的比亞韋斯托克-沃倫斯克方向入侵，迫使波軍兩線作戰。9月27日，華沙守軍在缺乏彈藥與飲水的情況下向德軍投降，標誌著首都陷落。10月6日，波蘭最後一個據點——莫德林要塞的守軍投降，標誌著正規戰鬥結束。兵力方面，德軍投入約880,000人，波蘭正規軍約450,000人，蘇聯則投入約500,000人；傷亡統計，德軍約45,000人（死亡、受傷及失踪），波蘭軍隊約66,000人死亡、130,000人受傷、420,000人被俘；蘇聯方面的傷亡較少，約5,000人。
dataEn: The chronology of the campaign is as follows: on 1 September 1939 at 04:45 the Germans first bombed the Westerplatte in the port of Gdańsk, then launched simultaneous ground offensives from East Prussia and Upper Silesia. On 3 September Britain and France declared war on Germany, but no major Western ground operations were undertaken immediately. On 8 September the 2nd Panzer Division of the German 4th Army reached the outskirts of Warsaw, beginning the Siege of Warsaw. From 14 to 19 September the Polish 7th and 15th Infantry Divisions fought fierce battles with German forces along the Bzura River, known as the Battle of the Bzura. On 17 September the Soviet Red Army invaded from the east along the Białystok‑Wołyńsk axis, forcing the Poles to fight on two fronts. On 27 September Warsaw’s garrison, lacking ammunition and water, surrendered to the Germans, marking the fall of the capital. On 6 October the last Polish stronghold, the Modlin fortress, surrendered, concluding regular combat operations. In terms of forces, the Germans deployed roughly 880,000 men, the Polish regular army about 450,000, and the Soviets about 500,000. Casualty figures are approximate: German losses about 45,000 (killed, wounded and missing), Polish losses about 66,000 dead, 130,000 wounded and 420,000 captured; Soviet casualties were far lower, around 5,000.
cause: 德國发动波蘭戰役的根本動機在於實現納粹意識形態中的「生存空間」概念，透過佔領波蘭走廊與但澤自由市，確保與東普魯士的陸地連接，並消除波蘭作為英法同盟的潛在橋頭堡。1939年4月，納粹-蘇聯簽署互不侵犯條約，並在秘密附加議定書中劃分了東歐勢力範圍，使德國在對波蘭動武時獲得蘇聯的中立保證。蘇聯則將波蘭東部的西白俄羅斯與西烏克蘭視為1917年革命後失去的領土，欲在德軍西進之際重新收回。兩國的共谋使波蘭陷入兩面夾擊的戰略劣勢。
causeEn: The fundamental motive for Germany’s invasion of Poland was to realize the Nazi concept of Lebensraum, seizing the Polish Corridor and the Free City of Danzig to secure a land link with East Prussia and to remove Poland as a potential springboard for an Anglo‑French alliance. In April 1939 Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed the non‑aggression pact, whose secret additional protocol divided Eastern Europe into spheres of influence, granting Germany Soviet neutrality in its war against Poland. The Soviet Union regarded the western parts of Belorussia and Ukraine—lost after the 1917 revolution—as territories to be reclaimed when the German advance opened the way. The collusion of the two powers placed Poland in a strategically untenable position of being attacked from both west and east.
impact: 波蘭戰役的結局直接促成英法於1939年9月3日對德宣戰，標誌著第二次世界大戰的正式爆發。儘管西線在此後數月未展開大規模地面行動，但德國在波蘭的成功展示了機械化兵團與空軍协同作战的威力，促使西方各國重新評估國防政策。蘇聯佔領波蘭東部後，將其纳入苏联西部边界，並在占領區展開集體化與政治清洗。戰役亦開啟了納粹對猶太人的系統性迫害，在波蘭領土上設立了首批集中營，如沃斯堡與奥斯威辛（後來更名）。波蘭流亡政府在英法的支持下繼續運作，組織了由波蘭士兵組成的西方軍團，最終在西方戰場發揮作用。
impactEn: The outcome of the Polish campaign directly prompted Britain and France to declare war on Germany on 3 September 1939, marking the official start of World II. Although no large‑scale Western ground operations followed for several months, Germany’s success in Poland demonstrated the decisive effect of coordinated mechanized forces and air power, forcing Western nations to rethink their defense strategies. After occupying eastern Poland, the Soviet Union incorporated the region into its western border and began collectivization and political purges in the occupied territories. The campaign also inaugurated the systematic Nazi persecution of Jews, establishing the first concentration camps on Polish soil, such as Auschwitz (later renamed) and others. The Polish government‑in‑exile, supported by Britain and France, continued to function and organized the Polish Armed Forces in the West, which later played significant roles on other fronts.
result: 最終，波蘭全境被德國與蘇聯瓜分：德國佔領西半部約20.4萬平方公里，設立了波蘭總督府；蘇聯則併入了東半部約20萬平方公里的土地，設置了西白俄羅斯與西烏克蘭蘇維埃社會主義共和國。從軍事角度看，德軍在此次戰役中損失約45,000人，消耗彈藥與燃料約300噸/師/日，展示了快速機動的作戰模式，但亦暴露出装甲师在高強度防禦中的消耗問題。波蘭軍隊的失敗主要源於裝備老舊、指揮結構的碎片化以及缺乏有效的空中掩護。儘管波蘭正規軍在10月初全數投降，隨後在西方與蘇聯境內形成的游擊隊與流亡軍隊持續對軸心國進行抵抗，直至戰爭結束。
resultEn: Ultimately, Poland was divided between Germany and the Soviet Union: Germany occupied the western half, roughly 204,000 km², establishing the General Government; the Soviet Union annexed the eastern half, about 200,000 km², creating the Belorussian and Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republics. From a military perspective, the Germans suffered roughly 45,000 casualties in the campaign and consumed about 300 tons of ammunition and fuel per division per day, showcasing the effectiveness of rapid, mobile warfare, but also revealing the vulnerability of armored divisions to sustained high‑intensity defense. The Polish army’s defeat stemmed mainly from obsolete equipment, fragmented command structures, and the lack of effective air cover. Although the regular Polish forces surrendered in early October, guerrilla groups and exile forces formed in the West and in Soviet territory continued to resist the Axis until the end of the war.
